The crime dataset contains the crime rate for each borough, while the adjacency dataset lists pairs of neighboring boroughs.

Next, we will create a spatial weights matrix based on the adjacency data. This matrix will indicate whether two boroughs are neighbors (1) or not (0). We will then standardize this matrix so that the weights sum to 1 for each borough.

After that, we will compute the Global Moran's I statistic. This statistic is calculated as the product of the spatial weights matrix and the deviation of the crime rate from its mean, divided by the variance of the crime rate. A positive Moran's I indicates that neighboring boroughs tend to have similar crime rates, while a value close to zero suggests that the crime rate is randomly distributed.
